SUMMARY Many patients with homozygous homocystinuria
develop severe premature atherosclerosis and thromboembolism, 
probably caused by abnormally high concentrations of homocyste-
ine.
Homocysteine undergoes metabolism either by remethylation 
or transsulfuration, and deficiency or dysfunction of any of the sub-
stances that regulate these reactions may lead to hyperhomocyste-
inemia.
Homocysteine may have adverse effects on platelets, 
clotting factors, and endothelial cells.
Studies have demonstrated 
significantly higher plasma homocysteine levels in patients with 
occlusive arterial disease than in controls.
The causes are not 
clearly understood but may include deficiency of vitamin B6,
vitamin B12, and folic acid and heterozygosity for cystathionine 
synthase deficiency.
Vitamin supplementation can lower plasma 
homocysteine levels.
